snippet.title: What If You Fell Out of a Plane Without a Parachute? 🪂
snippet.description:
You just fell out of a plane. No parachute. Good news: you've got about three minutes to think about your choices… 🪂 Starfish pose, skip the water, aim for snow. Two people actually survived falls like this.

Don't try this. Seriously.

FACT CHECK
• From ~10 km up, at around 200 km/h, the fall takes roughly three minutes; at that height the air is about -50°C and thin enough to make you pass out.
• Terminal velocity for a skydiver in the belly-down "starfish" position is about 200 km/h (~120 mph); spreading out increases drag.
• Nicholas Alkemade (1944): RAF tail gunner who jumped from his burning Lancaster at ~18,000 ft (~5.5 km) with no parachute; pine trees and deep snow broke his fall and he walked away with a sprained leg.
• Vesna Vulović (1972): flight attendant who survived a fall of 10,160 m inside a section of the aircraft; Guinness World Records lists it as the highest fall survived without a parachute.
